headline: AI agents can now live in your text messages, no app needed
summary: Forget downloading new apps; these AI assistants integrate directly into iMessage and SMS, handling tasks and managing information from your conversations.
details: A new wave of AI agents are bypassing traditional app interfaces, opting instead to reside within your existing text messaging platforms like iMessage and SMS. These agents can understand context, connect to your services, and perform tasks on your behalf, from scheduling appointments to managing family logistics.

Caddy, for instance, operates within iMessage on iPhones and RCS on Android, transforming scattered information from emails and texts into actionable items. It can add events to your calendar, set reminders, and even conduct research, all without requiring a separate application.

Fambot positions itself as a family's "chief of staff," organizing school communications, activities, and meal plans. Available via app and text, it sends daily summaries and allows parents to interact and make changes through simple replies. It plans to eventually charge a subscription fee comparable to Netflix.

Folk offers a similar texting interface through iMessage, WhatsApp, and Telegram, capable of managing reminders, researching topics, tracking flights, and making reservations. It runs on its own private cloud and can execute multi-step tasks. A Pro subscription is available for $8.33/month.

Instinct, a highly-valued AI agent, allows users to communicate via text or voice and connect to services like email and Google Workspace. It has begun offering dedicated email addresses for its assistants to manage sign-ups and communications, and is rolling out call placement capabilities.

Iris, powered by the Hermes agent, enables task delegation directly through iMessage. Users connect their apps and hand over tasks, with Iris working through the steps while retaining conversational context.
caption:
Your next personal assistant might just be a text message away. AI agents are ditching apps to live inside your SMS and iMessage.

headline_marked: [[AI agents use 5x more tokens]] than humans, driving HBM demand
headline: AI agents use 5x more tokens than humans, driving HBM demand
summary: AI agents are consuming significantly more tokens than humans, with projections indicating a tenfold increase, primarily driven by cached prompts. This trend is escalating demand for high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
details: AI agents are now using five times more tokens than humans on platforms like OpenRouter, according to data analyzed by Andreessen Horowitz. This usage has already surpassed human consumption, with projections suggesting it could reach ten times higher in the near future.

The vast majority of this agent token usage, over 85%, comes from cached prompts. This means AI agents are largely rereading previously processed information rather than generating entirely new content.

While cached tokens are less computationally expensive than processing new prompts from scratch, they still require significant memory resources. This sustained demand for memory is directly contributing to the increasing need for high-bandwidth memory (HBM).
The trend is not confined to a single platform. McKinsey's latest AI survey shows a significant increase in organizations scaling AI agents, indicating a broader industry shift towards agentic AI.

The growing demand for HBM, driven by AI's memory requirements, is already leading to shortages and price increases. Memory manufacturers are prioritizing AI data centers, potentially impacting availability and cost for PC consumers.
This escalating usage pattern suggests that while the cost per token might be lower due to caching, the underlying hardware costs, particularly for memory, remain substantial and are likely to grow.
